tasks.title: P28-01 - the client's own lifecycle: a pre-handshake close still retries, and close()/connect() leave nothing stale (D87, D93)
tasks.description: In `ibkr/client.py`, make `connectionClosed` schedule a reconnect in every state while keeping D40's classification inside `if was_connected:` - `was_connected = self._connected` and the `TWS_GONE` record stay exactly where they are, and `self._schedule_reconnect()` moves out of that branch so it runs after `_set_state(DISCONNECTED)` in every case; the docstring gains one sentence (a pre-handshake close is a transient failure: same backoff, no pause UI, no gap accounting, and `_schedule_reconnect`'s cancel-first contract is what keeps a `_poll`-armed backoff from duplicating). Make `close()` leave nothing stale: after the existing timer cancel, set `self._connection_state = ConnectionState.DISCONNECTED` DIRECTLY (not through `_set_state` - a deliberate close must not emit `disconnected` into `_on_disconnected` and run the outage path during teardown), then `self._last_disconnect_class = None`, `self._reconnect_attempt = 0`, `self._last_reconnect_log_delay = None`. Make `connect()` cancel a pending reconnect before storing params: if `self._reconnect_timer` is not None, `cancel()` and set it to None; `_do_reconnect` keeps calling `super().connect` (it must never cancel its own timer). New suite `tests/test_d87_d93_client_lifecycle.py` (fake transport, monkeypatched `threading.Timer` recorder). Do not change `_backoff_base`, `_max_backoff`, the exponent clamp, `_poll`'s handshake gate, `nextValidId`, `error`'s 502 suppression or any `DisconnectClass` value; do not touch `disconnect()`'s (EClient's) semantics or `closeEvent`'s call to it; add no signal and no timer. `tests/test_d27_reconnect.py`'s assertions stay untouched by this task (a later task adds the read-side test seam in that suite's window factory). Standing P28 constraints: `config/instance_lock.py` is the ONLY new module; no new dependency (QLockFile ships with PyQt6/QtCore); no migration and no `popouts` UNIQUE constraint (FI-P28-3); no settings key; no reconnect-policy change; D1-P27 unopened apart from the declared `[revises P4/P7/P13/P16]` labels; G5 is owner-run and is never claimed by a suite.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a client whose socket closes before `nextValidId`, When `connectionClosed` runs, Then a reconnect attempt is scheduled with the existing backoff and no state is left stopped-with-nothing-pending, and the drop is not recorded as `TWS_GONE`.

Given a connected client (handshake complete), When `close()` runs, Then `connection_state` is DISCONNECTED, no reconnect timer is pending, `_last_disconnect_class` is None, `_reconnect_attempt` is 0 and `_last_reconnect_log_delay` is None - and `close()` emits no `disconnected` signal (the outage path does not run in teardown).
Given a pending reconnect timer, When `connect()` is called, Then the pending timer is cancelled before any connection attempt and exactly one `super().connect` is issued.

Given a client whose handshake completed, When `connectionClosed` runs, Then D40's classification is unchanged: `_last_disconnect_class == DisconnectClass.TWS_GONE` and a reconnect is scheduled; and `_do_reconnect` still calls `super().connect` (it never cancels its own timer).

On a successful `ensure_rt_subscribed()` set `session._rt_attach_pending = False`. Add `def _attach_deferred_rt_feeds(self) -> None:` - for each session with `_rt_attach_pending` (iterate a copy): clear the flag, skip a 200-rejected contract, and call `_attach_live_feed(session.symbol, session._wave_contract or get_contract_for_symbol(session.symbol))`; call it in `_on_connected` immediately after `self._replay_subscriptions()`. 5. THE DROP OWES THE ATTACH (S-P28-2). `_rt_attach_pending` has exactly TWO setters: the readiness refusal above, and the drop. Extract `def _clear_prime_state(self) -> None:` in `ui/ticker_session.py` holding the six statements now copied THREE times - `self._prime_timer.stop()`, `self._prime_req_id = None`, `self._prime_period_start = None`, `self._prime_retry_pending = False`, `self._prime_retry_args = None`, `self._prime_reserved = False` - carrying the call sites' comments (Q-3/Q-12, P7-W2/S-P7-4) into the one docstring; `teardown`, `prepare_load` and `_fail_open_prime` each CALL IT IN PLACE OF their inline block and keep everything else and their order (teardown and prepare_load keep their surrounding resets; `_fail_open_prime` keeps `self._prime_skipped_count += 1`, its warning log and its `self._host._on_session_prime_complete(self)`). `teardown` additionally sets `self._rt_attach_pending = False` (the flag must not outlive the session). `_clear_prime_state()` has FOUR call sites: `teardown`, `prepare_load`, `_fail_open_prime`, `_on_disconnected`; the three-statement request transitions in `on_historical_data_end` / `on_historical_error` are exempt (they clear three statements and route an answer) - no OTHER full copy may remain. Then in `ui/main_window.py::_on_disconnected`, immediately BEFORE the stranded-wave loop - MARK FIRST, THEN CLEAR, because `_attach_live_feed` is the only other setter: `for session in list(self._sessions.values()): if (session._rt_req_id is None and session.symbol == self._current_symbol and (session._prime_timer.isActive() or session._prime_req_id is not None or session._prime_retry_pending)): session._rt_attach_pending = True` then `session._clear_prime_state()`, then `self._rt_retry_timer.stop()` with one comment (a pre-drop retry deadline must not act on a post-drop transport; the reconnect replay re-arms anything - S-P28-11). A 200-rejected contract needs no term here (`_attach_deferred_rt_feeds` already skips it and clears the flag). Existing flags are never cleared there. 7. Given `_rt_retry_timer` armed before a reconnect, When the reconnect completes (`_on_connected`), Then the timer is stopped, and firing the old callback issues no unsubscribe of the replayed reqId and no subscribe.

Given repeated errors arriving faster than the retry delay, When the delay elapses, Then exactly one retry fires at the originally scheduled instant: exactly one timer start at the first delay, the interval unchanged by later errors, `retry_attempt == 1`, and firing it issues exactly one subscribe.

Given errors beyond the attempt budget, When the last attempt fails, Then the stream stops retrying: state EXHAUSTED (distinct from FAILED), `retry_attempt == MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`, exactly one status line, `_rt_retry_timer` inactive, no subscribe on a later clock advance, and the badge reads the distinct terminal text.
